record.title: On-premise clinical agent paper reports consistency-gated selective autonomy in retrospective diagnostic simulations
record.summary: A Nature Medicine paper reports a fully on-premise clinical diagnostic agent with a behavioral-consistency measure used to select cases for autonomous handling in retrospective simulations. On 551 MIRA-v2 cases, the authors report that a 0.90 consistency threshold retained 49.4% of cases at 98.9% diagnostic accuracy (272 retained cases, three errors); the measured accuracy reflects a constructed MIMIC-IV-derived benchmark, not prospective clinical outcomes.
organizations: Else Kröner Fresenius Center for Digital Health

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report a fully on-premise clinical diagnostic agent evaluated on two MIMIC-IV-derived benchmarks, with 90.04% accuracy on a seven-disease task and 83.8% on a four-disease task; the paper says the primary benchmark result approached its cloud baseline.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that diagnostic behavioral consistency discriminated correctness with AUC 0.860 and remained informative under an information-scarcity stress test (AUC 0.875); at a 0.90 consistency threshold, 49.4% of 551 MIRA-v2 cases (272 cases) were retained at 98.9% accuracy, with three residual errors.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Nature Medicine paper is published and its indexed publisher record lists linked supplementary information and source-data files; this activation inspected indexed article text but did not download or independently analyze those data.

evidence_gaps.description: The publisher links full methods, supplementary information and source data that were not downloaded or inspected in this activation.
The results come from retrospective MIMIC-IV-derived simulations and do not establish prospective clinical safety, external validity, fairness or workload effects.
The operating point and AUCs were not independently reproduced in this activation.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported performance holds in clinical workflows, an on-premise diagnostic agent with a decision-time stability gate could offer hospitals a locally governed way to route a subset of cases for autonomous handling while deferring less stable cases. The consequence is meaningful for clinical AI system design, but evidence is retrospective and does not establish prospective safety or workload benefit.
limitations: The evaluation uses MIMIC-IV-derived diagnostic cases and simulated agent interactions; it is not a prospective clinical deployment or patient-outcome study.
The article reports a matched cloud baseline on the primary benchmark, but this activation did not inspect the full methods or baseline configuration in the article and supplements.

At the reported 0.90 ConsistencyDx threshold, 272 of 551 cases were retained at 98.9% accuracy, including three residual errors; this operating point is specific to the tested cohort and configuration.
The indexed article links supplementary material and source data, but those files were not downloaded or independently checked in this activation.
Local calibration, distribution shift, fairness, clinician workload, EHR integration and prospective safety remain unmeasured here.
organizations: Else Kröner Fresenius Center for Digital Health
brief.summary: A Nature Medicine paper reports a fully on-premise clinical diagnostic agent with a behavioral-consistency measure used to select cases for autonomous handling in retrospective simulations. On 551 MIRA-v2 cases, the authors report that a 0.90 consistency threshold retained 49.4% of cases at 98.9% diagnostic accuracy (272 retained cases, three errors); the measured accuracy reflects a constructed MIMIC-IV-derived benchmark, not prospective clinical outcomes.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 90.04% accuracy on a seven-disease task and 83.8% on a four-disease task. ConsistencyDx has AUC 0.860 and AUC 0.875 under stress testing; a 0.90 threshold retains 272/551 cases at 98.9% accuracy with three errors.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Nature Medicine paper and publisher-linked supplementary/source-data entries exist. The quantitative results remain paper-reported in this activation; no independent computation or reproduction was performed.
technical.mechanism: The paper describes a fully on-premise, two-agent diagnostic simulation and evaluates internal-likelihood, language-based and behavioral-stability signals. Diagnostic consistency across repeated runs is used as a gate to retain or defer cases.
technical.regime: Retrospective MIMIC-IV-derived benchmarks: MIRA-v2 seven-disease task (551 cases) and CDM four-disease task (2,400 cases), according to indexed source documentation. No live patient deployment was assessed in this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: The abstract says the on-premise agent approaches a cloud baseline on the primary benchmark; the thresholding comparison in the article text reports internal probability did not reach the same retained-case accuracy at evaluated thresholds. Exact comparator configuration was not inspected in full text.

brief.title: On-premise clinical agent paper reports consistency-gated selective autonomy in retrospective diagnostic simulations
brief.why_it_matters: Hospitals face a design choice between keeping clinical data under institutional control and using systems whose reliability varies by case. The paper reports a decision-time consistency signal that could support selective routing in the tested simulation. Whether it improves care or reduces clinician workload in practice is not established.
